Residual reactive gases may also form compounds or be solubalized in the liquid. Particularly pernicious in uranium alloys, for both reactivity and ubiquity in the atmosphere, are oxygen and nitrogen. Carbon sources tend to be incidental and are generally limited to backstreaming of oil from a vacuum pump, oils from handling (though gloves are always manditory), and improper cleaning of labeling from the charge materials (markers, crayons, etc.). All impurity introduction by these species and routes-of-entry would typically be measured at the ppm level during normal and proper operation. Button chemistry is summarized in Table 6. A single button did not meet what we would consider to be acceptable limits of uncertainty (~1%) due to an initial-to-final deviation of 5.6 grams, giving a maximum uncertainty of 1.624%. Measurements were still taken since there is redundant chemical sampling, but this point should remain more suspect than the others. DTA/TGA samples were nominally 3.5 mm dia and 1.00 mm thick. The final dimensions were not measured since the mass is captured by the instrument. Laser flash samples were 12.7 +/- 0.095 mm dia and 2 mm thick. Chemistry samples were extracted by drilling. All microscopy was performed post DTA as sections through the melted (and subsequently distorted) cylinders while still in the alumina sample cups. The same standard procedures for extracting drilled chemistry samples was followed as in S. Imhoff et al. (2020) with the exception that a 1/4” diameter bit was used.
